open_points.subject: owner-session locking across sessions
open_points.text: requests that read or change an uploaded file take the import lock before [the session lock] ... and other requests are not held by them
open_points.question: May a request in one owner session block uploaded-file requests in other sessions on the instance-wide import lock, or does the promise that other requests are not held exclude that?
options: The import lock serialises uploaded-file requests across all owner sessions
Only unrelated requests are not held; uploaded-file requests may be held
Each session must have independent import locking
open_points.default_guess: Treat the new import-lock rule as controlling: uploaded-file requests across sessions may block one another, while requests not using uploaded files do not.

open_points.subject: sign-out racing an already admitted uploaded-file request
open_points.text: A sign-out is applied in turn ... one admitted before it completes its change ... The requests ... are applied one at a time, in the order in which they take ... [their locks], after passing the session check
open_points.question: If an uploaded-file request passes the session check before sign-out but sign-out acquires the import and session locks first, must the earlier request still run before sign-out, be refused after sign-out, or be allowed to run against the ended session?
options: Admission order must be preserved through the locks
Lock-acquisition order controls and the request must recheck the session after acquiring both locks
A request admitted before sign-out may execute after sign-out against retained session state
open_points.default_guess: Recheck session validity after acquiring the locks and refuse a request if sign-out acquired them first.

open_points.subject: closure check versus upload validation
open_points.text: check the closure while holding them ... when the closure exists, uploading ... [is] refused
open_points.question: When the import is closed and an upload is also too large, unreadable, or otherwise invalid, is it refused for closure immediately, or does A04's global order require value validation before the lifecycle/closure check?
options: Closure is checked immediately after authentication and locking
A04 applies: validate the uploaded value before reporting closure
Closure is checked first internally but the externally visible refusal follows A04
open_points.default_guess: Refuse for closure before reading or validating the uploaded file, to avoid processing a file that can no longer be used.

open_points.subject: owner-only configuration completeness
open_points.text: one service token for each service ... or, for an owner-only start, none of the four ... every item of rule 1 present
open_points.question: Does the presence check require the four token variables in owner-only mode, and if so must they be absent, present empty, or represented by an explicit mode value?
options: All four token variables must be absent to select owner-only mode
All four variables must be present but empty
A separate explicit mode selects whether token variables are required
open_points.default_guess: Treat complete absence of all four token variables as owner-only mode; require all four nonempty tokens otherwise.

open_points.subject: configuration schema and validation
open_points.text: the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_ ... each well formed
open_points.question: What are the exact environment-variable names and lexical formats for the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential, and four service tokens, and what precisely makes each item malformed?
options: Specify fixed variable names and raw-string/path formats
Derive variable names from item and service names using an unstated naming convention
Let each implementation or release choose its own names and parsers
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed uppercase names derived from the listed items and services, interpret locations as filesystem paths, and treat secrets as literal UTF-8 strings.

open_points.subject: secret length and equality
open_points.text: A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long ... No two secrets are equal
open_points.question: How are environment-variable strings converted to bytes for the 32-byte test and constant-time comparison, and is distinctness tested on the supplied text, decoded bytes, or a normalized representation?
options: UTF-8 encode exactly as supplied and compare those bytes
Require a fixed encoding such as hexadecimal or base64 and compare decoded bytes
Count characters and compare configuration strings
open_points.default_guess: UTF-8 encode the exact supplied value with no normalization, then test length and equality on those bytes.

open_points.subject: backup encryption and key fingerprint
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key ... and a digest of the key it was made with
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption construction, nonce generation, key derivation or key-size rule, file authentication, and key-digest algorithm and representation must a backup use?
options: A specified authenticated-encryption format using the configured bytes directly as a fixed-size key
A specified KDF derives an encryption key from the configured secret, followed by authenticated encryption
Each implementation chooses its own encryption and digest schemes
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption container, derive a fixed-size key with a specified KDF, use a fresh random nonce, and record a SHA-256 fingerprint of the derived key.

open_points.subject: backup filenames, prefixes and cleartext record
open_points.text: Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares ... A kept name is made from the backup's instant ... it records, readable without its key
open_points.question: What are the exact prefixes, timestamp precision and filename encoding, and the syntax and validation rules of the unencrypted backup record that governs scheduling, display, retention and deletion?
options: State 2 fixes one versioned filename and metadata format
State 6 fixes the internal backup format
Each release may choose any format while preserving the listed facts
open_points.default_guess: Define a fixed versioned metadata header and UTC timestamp filename with microsecond precision, plus release-fixed distinct temporary and kept prefixes.

open_points.subject: failure during backup checking and cleanup
open_points.text: it decrypts it into a second temporary file, opens that ... checks ... and removes it; a backup that passes is renamed to its kept name, one that fails is deleted. Third, whatever the second step did ...
open_points.question: If checking succeeds but removal of the decrypted temporary file fails, or cleanup of a failed candidate fails, is the encrypted backup kept, deleted, or left temporary, and does retention step three still run?
options: Any check-step cleanup failure prevents keeping the backup but retention still runs
A successfully checked encrypted backup is kept even if plaintext cleanup fails, and the run is reported failed
Any such failure stops the run before retention
open_points.default_guess: Do not keep the backup unless the decrypted temporary file was removed successfully; leave only removable temporary files, report failure, and still perform retention step three.
